captions.detailed: This 3D model presents a multi-part, 3D-printable fastener system consisting of four distinct half-sections laid out in a row. The first two parts are half-cores, each featuring a semi-circular flat head and a thin, solid cylindrical shaft extending from its flat side. The remaining two parts are matching half-outers, which feature a larger semi-circular head and a hollow sleeve designed to slide over the core's shaft. All four pieces are split along their longitudinal axes, allowing them to be printed flat on the build plate without supports.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric, 3D-printable Chicago-style screw fastener split into halves for easy printing. The design should generate two core halves with thin solid pins, and two outer sleeve halves with matching internal channels, allowing adjustable parameters for head diameter, head height, sleeve length, outer diameter, and fit tolerance (play).
captions.factory: The script defines two main modules: 'core' and 'outter', both constructed using CSG operations. In the 'core' module, a union of two cylinders rotated along the Y-axis forms the head and the inner pin, which is then halved by subtracting a large cube. Similarly, the 'outter' module unions a larger sleeve cylinder and a head cylinder, subtracts an internal cylinder for the sleeve channel with added 'Play' tolerance, and utilizes a subtracting cube to slice the assembly in half. Four instances (two cores and two outers) are translated along the X-axis for a complete printable set.
